svg.text: The queue is not what limits Norwegian salmon
Maximum allowed biomass in tonnes. More licensed capacity is sitting with no fish in it than the entire pending queue
is asking for — by a factor of 3.4.
This recipe previously said licensed biomass caps output, so the queue binds growth. The first half is true and the second does not follow.

text.tspan: 1.44 million tonnes of licensed capacity has no fish in it, against 431 thousand tonnes waiting to be licensed.

svg.text: The queue is real, slow and getting slower — but licence availability is not what caps production, because most of what is already licensed is not in use.
Idle does not mean available. Salmon sites are deliberately fallowed between production cycles, so an unknown share of these 464 sites is a working farm between crops rather than dormant
capacity. This chart rules out one explanation; it does not establish the replacement.

Counted only where the licence states tonnes. The field also carries STK, a count of individual fish, and DA, an area — summing those as mass gave 87 million tonnes against a national output near 1.5 million.
Sources: Fiskeridirektoratet Akvakultursøknader and Biomasse layers.
